title: Maker markout census: what every resting order that actually traded earned to the SP, with no queue model at all
definition: From the stream, take every increment of traded volume at a price in the last 300 s (and after the scheduled off) of each WIN market and classify the resting side by the book just before it: a print at the prevailing best back price means a resting layer was filled, at the best lay price a resting backer. Compute the volume-weighted maker return to the SP for each print (resting back at L: L/SP - 1; resting lay: 1 - L/SP) and tabulate it by seconds to the off (10 s buckets), price band, spread in ticks, track and runner rank, with the quoted half-spread beside it. The output is a map of spread earned per unit of adverse selection for the average maker, and a walk-forward cell selector (quote only in cells positive on all earlier days after shrinkage to the pooled mean).
data_needed: Held: Exchange Stream from 5 Nov (traded volume per price, full ladder, the settled SP in the market definition), replayed by research/greyhound/stream_replay.events/apply. Unverified: whether a stream trade increment counts one side or both (stream_replay's vol_factor note); the census is a volume-weighted mean so the answer does not change it.
mechanism: Every resting-order result so far depends on a simulated queue. The census needs none: the prints are real fills of real makers, so their average return to the SP is a fact about this market. If the average maker in a cell loses to the SP, no queue position rescues joining there; if it earns more than commission, the question reduces to queue position (maker-05, maker-09). It also answers 'which markets and minutes have the widest spread per unit of adverse selection' directly, something the 60 s and 0 s checkpoints cannot.
nearest_tried: greyhound-edge-anatomy-1111 (L714) measured takers at fixed checkpoints on the live-key books (taken with no signal, closed at the SP: all negative); ES family 13 simulates our own orders. Nothing has measured the realised return of the makers who were actually filled.

title: Two-part order-value model: P(fill) x E[log(price/SP) | fill], trained on the replay's own all-runner orders
definition: Take every rest_back_60_all and rest_lay_60_all order the nightly close lab already replays (one row a runner-side at 60 s) as training rows: label 1 = matched share > 0, label 2 = pnl_sp per unit matched. Fit walk-forward by day two LightGBM models on the checkpoint's frame columns (close_lab FEATURES families book, flow, sp, race, path, sppool), the forecast gap log(forecast SP/mid) from gbm_small_plus_huber, spread in ticks, queue_at_place, and queue_at_place over tv_d60: a binary P(fill) and a Huber regression of pnl_sp on filled rows only. The rule rest_back_60_ev / rest_lay_60_ev places an order only when P(fill) x E[pnl | fill] is above zero (and a second cut at the top third), scored on later days by the same replay.
data_needed: Held: close_lab cached frames (frames_v2) and the cached rest_v1 replay rows per day (close_lab/rest_v1_<hash>/<day>.parquet) from the stream days 5 Nov on. rest_day currently drops queue_at_place, first_fill and via_through from sr.replay's output; they must be kept (a column change, no new data).
mechanism: The m0/m3 gates select on the unconditional forecast of the SP, but a resting order's return is the SP move conditional on being filled, and fills are the adverse half of the distribution (live lays matched +0.0175 log SP/price, unmatched +0.3511, L820). A model whose target is already conditioned on the fill learns which book states give fills that are not informed - the thing the close forecast cannot see by construction.

No new replay is needed for the first read because the 'all' variants already hold an order for every eligible runner; 4 rules (2 sides x 2 cuts) registered before the run.

title: The fill bracket as the forward gate for rest_back_60_m0: front of queue, queue as shown, through-only, each with latency
definition: Pre-register the forward read of rest_back_60_m0 (days from 19 Nov, unchanged orders) as four fills of the same orders instead of one: FRONT (queue_ahead forced to 0 - the best any maker could do), SHOWN (rest_v1 as now), THROUGH (the order fills only from volume traded strictly beyond its price, capped at that volume - every lot at our price is assumed to go to others; this is the resting analogue of the 'through' fill, the only fill trusted against live in fill_recon), and THROUGH with the order entered 1 s late. A pass requires the THROUGH arm's pnl_sp at the SP to have its 90% by-day interval above zero and a deflated Sharpe of at least 0.95 with the family's trials read from the ledger; SHOWN and FRONT are reported as the upside, never as the gate.
data_needed: Held: Exchange Stream forward days from 19 Nov (the locked holdout), close_lab frames and the gbm_small_plus forecast; research/overfit.dsr_check. The trial count must come from the ledger (ES family 13: 12 rules x 2 targets, plus every maker variant registered in this round) - the map notes no single ledger-derived count exists yet (W5).
mechanism: Every greyhound rule so far passed on the optimistic fill and failed on the one a live order gets (map W4), and rest_back_60_m0's +1.259% (1,652 trades, 90% 0.593 to 1.771) is on a queue fill never validated against live. Bracketing turns an unverifiable point estimate into bounds: if the rule survives when it is credited only with fills where the price went through it, queue position cannot be what makes it pay; if it survives only as SHOWN, the edge is the queue assumption. It also stops the 10-day 'candidate' label from being read as a pass without the deflated Sharpe the owner's rule requires.

title: Join, improve or sit one level back: queue position as the decision at placement
definition: For each rest_back_60_m0 order build three alternatives on the same runner and second: JOIN (price = best lay l1, as now), IMPROVE (price = trading.exchange.tick_down(l1) when that is still above the best back b1, i.e. the spread is two ticks or more; queue ahead is then zero in SimOrder.place) and BACK-ROW (price = l2, one level further from the mid). Replay all three through stream_replay with through_cap=True, to_close=True and report per order placed (not per matched order) pnl_sp, matched share and share filled via trade-through. The rule chosen is a function of spread in ticks only: improve when spread >= 3 ticks, join otherwise.
data_needed: Held: Exchange Stream full ladder from 5 Nov (the stream gives every level, so l2 and the empty inside ticks are known); close_lab frames (b1-b3, l1-l3 with sizes); trading/exchange.py tick_up/tick_down (read-only import in research code).
mechanism: At the touch our order is last in a queue whose front is filled by uninformed flow and whose back is filled only when the level is cleared - the adverse case. Improving by one tick gives up one tick of price to be first for all flow; sitting a level back earns more but fills only on sweeps. Greyhound ladders are coarse relative to the price (wide tick spreads at 3-10), so the trade-off is large and has never been measured here. title: Residual softmax on the BSP offset, monotone in the price, served as limit-on-close limits (S1 sharpened)
definition: LightGBM with the race softmax objective (greyhound/fastloop.py race_soft_objective) and init_score = log(BSP share), so the trees learn only log(p/q); target the winner, with a second arm on the top-two exploded likelihood (pl2) carrying the same offset. Features: the card-safe columns plus log BSP share and BSP rank, a monotone constraint on log BSP share, low capacity (15 leaves, at least 2,000 rows a leaf, early-stopped on the next year's race log-loss), walk-forward by year over every fully priced race 2018-2026. Because the fitted edge is monotone in the dog's own SP, each dog gets one limit: the lowest SP at which the edge clears the commission hurdle 0.02 x (1 - q) plus a registered margin is a limit-on-close back limit (the highest SP for a lay), so the order needs no knowledge of the SP.

definition: Define for an order at the touch queue_turn = queue_at_place / max(trailing 60 s traded volume on that runner at or through that side of the book, 1), i.e. how many 'minutes of flow' stand ahead of us, and level_age = seconds since the touch price last changed. The rule rest_back_60_m0_qt places the m0 back only when queue_turn is below the earlier days' median (we reach the front while the flow is still ordinary), and reports the complement beside it. title: A race-level temper: which races are more random than their SP book says
definition: One scalar a race, tau = exp(g(z)), with p_i proportional to q_i^tau and q the BSP share; g reads race-level inputs only: early-pace pressure and collision chance (sm2_ crowding, ln2_ pace collision, bd2_), the count of debutants and of dogs under 3 runs (rx_n_debut, rx_n_lt3), field size, vacant traps, trip class, grade and the spread of ratings. Fitted by the race's log-likelihood in log tau (first as tau = exp(w.z), then LightGBM with the gradient repeated on the race's rows). Rule: tau under 1 - a - a limit-on-close lay of the SP favourite; tau over 1 + a - a market-on-close back of the favourite, where the hurdle 0.02 x (1 - q) is lowest.
data_needed: The fast-loop cache from 1 Jun 2020 with pit tables sim2, line2, bend2, racectx; the BSP and results - held.
mechanism: A favourite's price sums up ability; whether ability gets a clear run is settled at the first bend, which is a property of the race and not of the dog. Punters price dogs one at a time, so a crowded-bend race can carry a favourite too short and a one-pace race a favourite too long.

Differs: the target is the result with the BSP as base and the input is the race's shape.

title: Place SP against the dog's experience: the debutant's fat tail
definition: For every GB runner with both a win BSP and a place BSP, compute Harville's place chance from the win BSPs of the race and the realised place A/E at the place BSP, by experience cell known on the card (runs before = 0, 1-2, 3+; `db_w` in greyhound/pit/debut.py). The rule is card-only: back or lay at the place SP every runner in a cell (no price condition, so no look-ahead on the SP), 6 rules in all (3 cells x 2 sides). A dog with no form has a wider spread of outcomes than its win price implies under Harville, so its place chance should sit below Harville's; the test is whether the place SP already carries that discount.

title: The BSP book-sum harvest: dutch the field at the SP when the SP book is forecast under 100%
definition: Let B = sum of 1/BSP over a race's runners. Forecast B from what is known 10 s before the off: the sums of 1/spn and 1/spf, each runner's SP pool imbalance, field size, vacant traps, track, hour and traded volume. Where the forecast is under 1 - h (h in {0.02, 0.03}) back every runner at the SP (market-on-close) with stakes proportional to the forecast shares, which returns 1/B - 1 before commission in expectation whatever wins; where it is over 1 + h lay every runner at the SP with liability s x (1 - share).
data_needed: Price files give B for every fully priced race 2018-2026 (its distribution by track, field and year: no data found in the reports read); the stream from 5 Nov gives the forecast's inputs - held.
mechanism: Each runner's BSP is reconciled on its own; nothing forces the book to 100% and nobody can arbitrage the sum after the off, so a thin greyhound SP pool leaves race-level slack. A dutch pays in every race, so its variance is low and 15 days of stream have power where a win-settled single bet has none.

Differs: this dutch reads no form model, only the predicted book sum.

(b) close_lab.py frames: forecast B at the last checkpoint, walk-forward by day, and score the rule with 2% on each market's net; a bound of zero in (a) closes the idea in one run.

title: The track tonight: a same-meeting trap and rail bias state
definition: For race k, from the meeting's earlier races (off at least 10 minutes before): per trap, winners less BSP-expected winners so far, shrunk by a prior weight fitted on early years; collapsed to an inside-minus-outside index (traps 1-2 against 5-6) and a favourite index (favourites' wins less expected). mechanism: Sand condition changes through a meeting (watering, harrowing, rain: wx_ reads weather at the off, not what the track has done since race 1), and it shows first as a rail or wide bias. Regulars at the track see it; the exchange crowd pricing from the card may not.

title: Rest in the PLACE book at the win book's implied place price
definition: At 60 s before the off compute each dog's place fair price from the WIN book mids: Harville with a discount exponent per field size fitted once on the price files (place BSP against win BSP, years before 2026). Rest a back in the PLACE book at fair x (1 + m), m in {0, 3%}, and a lay at fair x (1 - m), only where that price is at or outside the place book's best quote; an order that fills is closed at the place SP, an unfilled one cancelled at the off. Four rules, scored queue-aware.
data_needed: Held: Exchange Stream WIN and PLACE ladders from 5 Nov (greyhound/stream_record.py), place and win BSP history for the discount fit. Nothing missing; place-book depth at 60 s is unmeasured in the repo - no data found.
mechanism: The win book is where the money and the information arrive; the place book is thinner and its quotes are refreshed less often, so a place quote can be stale against a win price that has just moved. A resting order there is a maker in the market with fewer makers, the side of W4 that has shown life (rest_back_60_m0 +1.259% at the SP, map W4).

ES family 13 rests in the WIN book; close_lab.features() keeps WIN runners and reads the place market only as p_vs_win. No resting order has been simulated in the PLACE book.

title: The non-runner shock: who really gains when a dog comes out

Our pipeline drops these races entirely (greyhound/tradeout.py; roadmap J4 open), so they have never been priced or tested.

title: Fade the SP's reconciliation jump: limit-on-close orders either side of the last micro-price
definition: At the last stream message at least 10 s before the real off, take each runner's size-weighted micro-price m (close_lab._mid). Place a limit-on-close back with limit m x (1 + k) and a limit-on-close lay with limit m x (1 - k), k in {0.05, 0.10}: each fills at the BSP only if the BSP lands beyond its limit, and is settled by the result. Gate arm: only where the SP pool imbalance (close_lab sp_imb) points the same way. Before any rule, one reading: a conditional logit of the winner on log BSP share plus d = log(BSP / m); a coefficient on d below zero says the jump is noise.
data_needed: Exchange Stream from 5 Nov (ladder, spn, spf, spb, spl) and live-key books from 3 Nov (sp_near, sp_far, sp_actual) - held, about 15 days, so the result-settled reading is low powered and must accrue forward days from 19 Nov.
mechanism: The BSP is struck per runner from the SP back and lay pools plus whatever unmatched orders are left. In a thin pool one trader closing at the SP (as our own early-lay close does) moves it away from the book's consensus, and that hedging flow knows nothing about the result. A limit-on-close order collects only when the jump happens and has an exact fill.

Differs: the SP is the entry, not the exit; the fill is exact; the question is whether the SP or the last book is the better chance.

title: Race books at the SP that net the commission: stake-fixed backs, liability-fixed lays and the synthetic lay
definition: Given residual chances p and a forecast of the BSP shares, choose for each race SP back stakes b_i and SP lay liabilities l_i that maximise expected log growth net of 0.02 x E[max(market net, 0)] under a per-race exposure cap; commission is on the market's net, so offsetting legs in one race cut it. Two exact forms of a lay are compared: (a) a lay by liability, whose stake floats as L / (BSP - 1) and grows when the dog shortens, and (b) the synthetic lay, backing the other runners at the SP in proportion to their forecast shares, cheaper when the SP book sums under 100% (sp-05). Sizes come from a Monte Carlo over the forecast's error in log BSP (RMSE 0.2759, baseline_v0).
data_needed: The selections of a residual model that has passed (sp-01, sp-02, sp-05); BSP and results; greyhound/costs.py - held once a signal exists.
mechanism: A single back at share q pays 0.02 x (1 - q) of its stake in commission; a netted book pays less per unit of edge, and an edge of 1-2% lives or dies on that. The size of an SP bet is random because the price is unknown when the order goes in, which the Kelly ladder for known prices ignores.
nearest_tried: L815 whole-race structures (dutches, pairs, a Kelly book: 0 of 28), all priced from the BSP forecaster's value with commission applied after the fact. Differs: sizing with the SP unknown and commission inside the objective; it is not a signal and is only run on a signal that has passed.

title: A bar in standard errors: posterior edge by normal-normal shrinkage at the decision book
definition: New arm eb_post in research/greyhound/edge_models.py: for each runner e = log(back1 / forecast SP) and sigma_i = the runner's forecast-error SD at the decision book (the uncert-01 quantile fit refitted on live-key race-traded rows with log price, spread, matched volume, seconds to the off and field size). Posterior mean edge m_i = w_i x e_i with w_i = tau2 / (tau2 + sigma_i^2), tau2 the method-of-moments variance of true edge on the training days (var(e) - mean sigma^2, floored at zero). A back is taken only when the posterior chance of a positive edge after the 2% commission is at least 0.90; if tau2 fits to zero the arm takes nothing, and that is the reading.
data_needed: Held: live-key books from 3 Nov, recorder books from 6 Oct, served and out-of-sample prices. Nothing missing.
mechanism: A fixed 8% or 3% bar picks the runners where the forecast is most wrong (SP 16-19% over the forecast on the taken backs, L992). Shrinking each gap by its own reliability makes a loose forecast need a proportionally larger gap and pulls the predicted edge on taken bets down to what can be realised.
